Erik Ninn-Hansen (22 September 1922 – 12 September 2014) was a Danish politician who served as a member of the Danish Parliament (Folketing) and held several ministerial positions in the Danish government. He was a prominent figure in the Venstre (Liberal Party) and is most notably remembered for his role in the **"Tamil Case" (Tamilsagen)**, a major political scandal in Denmark that led to his resignation and legal consequences.

### **Early Life and Political Career**
- Born in **Randers, Denmark**, Ninn-Hansen studied law and became a lawyer before entering politics.
- He was first elected to the Folketing in **1957** as a member of Venstre.
- Over the years, he held various positions, including **Minister of Justice (1968–1971)** and **Minister of Defence (1973–1975)**.

### **Minister of Justice and the Tamil Case (1986–1989)**
Ninn-Hansen is best known for his controversial tenure as **Minister of Justice (1982–1988)** under **Poul Schlüter’s** conservative-liberal government. The **"Tamil Case" (Tamilsagen)** was a major scandal that emerged in 1989, revealing that Ninn-Hansen had **illegally delayed family reunification for Sri Lankan Tamil refugees** to discourage further asylum applications.

#### **Key Details of the Tamil Case:**
- In **1987**, Ninn-Hansen **ordered immigration officials to delay processing family reunification requests** from Tamil refugees who had been granted asylum in Denmark.
- The policy was intended to **deter more Tamils from coming to Denmark** by making it harder for them to bring family members.
- The scandal broke in **1989** when internal documents were leaked, showing that Ninn-Hansen had **overruled legal advice** and actd in a discriminatory manner.
- The **Danish Parliament’s Ombudsman** ruled that Ninn-Hansen’s actions were **unlawful**, violating Denmark’s **Aliens Act** and international human rights obligations.
- The case led to a **vote of no confidence** in Ninn-Hansen, forcing his resignation in **June 1989**.
- It also **weakened Prime Minister Poul Schlüter’s government**, contributing to Venstre’s decline in the late 1980s.

### **Legal Aftermath and Conviction**
- In **1995**, after a long legal battle, the **Danish Supreme Court (Højesteret)** ruled that Ninn-Hansen had **acted unlawfully** by instructing officials to delay Tamil family reunifications.
- He was **fined 25,000 DKK** (approx. **€3,350** at the time) for **abuse of power**, making him the **first Danish minister ever convicted for actions taken in office**.
- The case set a **precedent in Danish administrative law**, reinforcing that ministers must follow the law and cannot issue informal, discriminatory instructions.

### **Later Life and Death**
- After resigning, Ninn-Hansen remained active in Venstre but never returned to a ministerial position.
- He continued as a **Folketing member until 1994** before retiring.
- He died on **12 September 2014**, just 10 days before his 92nd birthday.

### **Legacy**
- The **Tamil Case** remains one of the most **infamous political scandals in Danish history**, often cited in debates about **immigration policy, ministerial accountability, and the rule of law**.
- It contributed to **stricter oversight of ministers** and reinforced the principle that **government officials cannot bypass laws** for political convenience.
- Some critics argue that Ninn-Hansen was a **scapegoat** for broader government policies, while others see the case as a **necessary check on executive power**.
